title: SpectrePrefetch: Undermining Cache-Centric Secure Speculation with Modern Hardware Prefetchers
problem: Cache-centric secure speculation defenses fail to address security vulnerabilities exploitable through hardware prefetchers during speculative execution. Prefetchers can become transmission media for leaking secrets through their patterns and confidence signals.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating transient execution attacks that exploit hardware prefetchers is critical for securing modern CPUs against information leakage through speculative execution paths.
method: CPUs execute code speculatively—running instructions before confirming they're actually needed—and during this time, hardware prefetchers (the parts that guess which memory data you'll need next) accidentally reveal secrets. SpectrePrefetch exploits this by encoding secrets into how the prefetchers behave, then extracting those secrets in two ways: by reading the memory-access patterns the prefetchers leave in the cache, or by reading the confidence levels stored inside the prefetcher. The attacks were tested on Intel processors and a detailed simulator (Gem5), and researchers also proposed a defense using randomized prefetching that maintains normal performance.
key_novelty: This is the first framework to exploit hardware prefetchers as hidden information leaks (covert channels) during speculative execution, showing that cache-based defenses against speculative attacks are insufficient.
contributions: Attack framework demonstrating secret leakage through prefetching patterns and confidence at 31.25 Kbps with 98.87% accuracy
Theoretical and empirical evidence that prefetchers defeat cache-centric secure speculation defenses
Analysis showing that restrictive defenses like MuonTrap lose substantial performance benefits
Low-cost non-deterministic prefetching defense maintaining average performance on SPEC2017 benchmarks

metrics.other: 31.25 Kbps secret leakage bandwidth; maintained average performance

limitations: Evaluation limited to specific Intel CPU models and simulation; generalization to other CPU architectures and more advanced prefetchers is not explored.
primary_theme: Prefetcher-based covert channel in speculative execution
